messages:
sam: Heads up — edge probes started ejecting eu-west zones for user-facing routes ~10m ago, seeing a spike in 5xxs and routed traffic weirdness. any thoughts?

dylan: noticed it too. looks like probe_fail_count went from 2 -> 6 in a minute. is probe TTL still 30s? seems short.

alex: yeah 30s is aggressive, causes quick ejection during short blips. i recommend bumping probe_ttl_seconds to 120 and adding a cool-down window to avoid flapping.

maria: curious — are we ejecting based on probe failures only or combining with latency thresholds? we discussed a combined signal in the last oncall doc.

sam: current policy: probe failures OR 95th latency > 500ms for 2 consecutive windows. but for small zones with low qps probe noise dominates.

alex: proposal: change precedence to: 1) sustained latency breaches, 2) probe failures with TTL 120s + 3 consecutive failures, 3) manual ejection via console. also add a grace TTL after reinstate.

maria: sounds good. also we need to consider affinity — sticky headers like X-RW-Region-Prefer are used by some partners. if we eject, sticky headers should still honor preference unless route policy overrides.

sam: important callout: mobile SDKs don't set cookies reliably, so header-based affinity is preferred for app clients. but browsers + CDN caching behave better with cookie affinity.

alex: sug code/config example i was thinking: 
```
route_routing: 
  precedence: [header, cookie, geoip] 
  affinity_headers: ["X-RW-Region-Prefer", "X-Prefer-Region"] 
  cookie_name: "rw_region" 
  probe_ttl_seconds: 120
  probe_fail_threshold: 3
  latency_fallback_ms: 250 # 95th pct threshold
```

dylan: love the precedence ordering. one more: add an "ejection_safety_margin" so that if a region is partially degraded we shift weights gradually instead of full cutover. e.g., reduce weight by 30% then evaluate.

maria: yes — console UX should expose current weight modifiers and a timeline. ops wants an actionable "take region offline" button that triggers controlled drain and a rollback path.

sre-ops: runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/region-ejection ; recommend follow steps 2-4 (verify probes, check inter-region links, bump TTL).

deploy-bot: deploy started by @ci on branch region/probe-ttl-update (sha: ab12cd)

sam: quick question re: header vs cookie precedence — in our gateway matching, do we rewrite headers for internal calls? we used to strip X-RW-* for non-edge to prevent header spoofing.

alex: we still strip at internal ingress. plan: allow X-RW-* at edge only and sign them (HMAC) so we can trust them across internal hops. header becomes X-RW-Region-Prefer: eu-west; X-RW-Sig: <sig>.

maria: sign+verify is ideal. ops can rotate signing key via KMS. add to privacy doc.

dylan: also think about cache TTLs on CDN — if we change routing quickly, cached responses might be served from wrong region. we should surface cache invalidation hooks in the rollout.

sam: ok i've got action items: open PR to bump probe_ttl + safety margin, add precedence config, and a console card for "region affinity weights". i'll link the PR here when ready.

maria: assigning to eng-platform board and slack thread for tracking. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/region/probe-ttl-update — draft created. will add tests for signed header handling.

sre-ops: following up in runbook after deploy completes. keep monitoring 5xx and p95 latency.

alex: LGTM, ping me for the HMAC key rotation bits.

sam: closing loop — will roll this out as canary to 5% of traffic then 25% then 100%. will post metrics checkpoints.
